## Your destination

Use LD-pruned variants to calculate principal components, inspect possible
structure and batch effects, join sample information safely, and build an
explicit, reproducible sample list for the association models.

**Core walkthrough:** sections 1–6. Keep your interpretation of each plot beside
your code. **Going further:** reference panels, cohort restriction and HWE filters.

## Start from the checkpoint

Restart R. Open the project before running this first chunk.

```{r pca-setup}
root <- if (file.exists("R/course.R")) "." else ".."
source(file.path(root, "R", "course.R"))
cfg <- course_config(root)
input <- file.path(cfg$qc, "qc_final")
print(check_bed(input))
metadata <- load_metadata(cfg)
```

**Check your result:** QC files are present in the same data mode you used in
lesson 1. If you are rejoining the class, use the checkpoint instructions in
[troubleshooting](../../docs/troubleshooting.md#rejoining-the-class).

## Choose the study samples and prune variants

A PCA cluster is a genetic similarity pattern. Without appropriate reference
data it is not a validated ancestry label. `Group` comes from the supplied
metadata; do not assume that it means ancestry or recruitment centre.
Demo `Group` values are the two frequency groups used by the simulator.

The default walkthrough retains all post-QC samples for an exploratory analysis.
If an analysis cohort has been agreed after reviewing the data, put its FID/IID
file in `course_settings$analysis_keep` and rerun lessons 2 and 3. Do not choose a
cohort by whichever selection produces the most significant association.

```{r pca-analysis-cohort}
cohort <- file.path(cfg$pca, "analysis_cohort")
args <- c("--bfile", input)
if (nzchar(cfg$analysis_keep)) {
  keep_path <- file.path(cfg$root, cfg$analysis_keep)
  keep <- read_ws(keep_path, header = FALSE)
  if (ncol(keep) != 2L) stop("analysis_keep must have two headerless columns: FID IID.")
  names(keep) <- c("FID", "IID")
  check_ids(keep, "Analysis cohort list")
  if (!all(id_key(keep) %in% id_key(read_fam(input)))) stop("Analysis list contains unknown QC sample IDs.")
  args <- c(args, "--keep", keep_path)
}
run_plink(cfg, c(args, "--make-bed", "--out", cohort))
prune <- file.path(cfg$pca, "prune")
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", cohort, "--maf", "0.05", "--indep-pairwise", "200", "50", "0.2",
                "--out", prune), paste0(prune, ".prune.in"))
cat("LD-pruned variants:", length(readLines(paste0(prune, ".prune.in"))), "\n")
```

**Try it yourself — Q4:** why use an LD-pruned subset to estimate structure, but
retain a larger set of variants for association testing?

## Calculate PCs and inspect the eigenvalues

```{r pca-calculate}
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", cohort, "--extract", paste0(prune, ".prune.in"),
                "--maf", "0.05", "--pca", cfg$n_pcs, "meanimpute", "scols=fid",
                "--out", file.path(cfg$pca, "study")),
          file.path(cfg$pca, c("study.eigenvec", "study.eigenval")))
pcs <- read_pcs(cfg)
eigenvalues <- scan(file.path(cfg$pca, "study.eigenval"), quiet = TRUE)
head(pcs)
```

```{r pca-scree, fig.alt="Scree plot of the eigenvalues for the principal components calculated in this lesson."}
plot(seq_along(eigenvalues), eigenvalues, type = "b", pch = 16,
     xlab = "Principal component", ylab = "Eigenvalue", main = "Returned PCA eigenvalues")
```

**Check your result:** FID, IID and PC columns are present. Only the requested
eigenvalues are returned. Dividing each by the sum of these values gives its share
of the returned components, not its share of total genome-wide variance.
We plot the eigenvalues directly.

## Join by identifiers, then plot

**The question:** does structure overlap with phenotype or recorded groups?

```{r pca-join}
plot_data <- join_by_id(pcs, metadata)
table(plot_data$Disease, plot_data$Group, useNA = "ifany")
```

```{r pca-scatter, fig.alt="PC1 versus PC2 shown twice, first with case/control symbols and then with symbols for the recorded metadata groups."}
status <- factor(plot_data$Disease, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Control", "Case"))
status_code <- as.integer(status)
status_code[is.na(status_code)] <- 3L
groups <- factor(ifelse(is.na(plot_data$Group), "Missing", plot_data$Group))
draw_pca <- function() {
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
  plot(plot_data$PC1, plot_data$PC2, pch = c(1, 17, 4)[status_code],
       col = c("#174A67", "#A34B18", "#555555")[status_code], xlab = "PC1", ylab = "PC2", main = "Phenotype")
  legend("topright", c("Control", "Case", "Missing"), pch = c(1, 17, 4),
         col = c("#174A67", "#A34B18", "#555555"), bty = "n", cex = 0.7)
  group_code <- as.integer(groups)
  plot(plot_data$PC1, plot_data$PC2, pch = 1 + (group_code - 1) %% 6,
       col = hcl.colors(nlevels(groups), "Dark 3")[group_code],
       xlab = "PC1", ylab = "PC2", main = "Recorded group")
  legend("topright", levels(groups), pch = 1 + (seq_len(nlevels(groups)) - 1) %% 6,
         col = hcl.colors(nlevels(groups), "Dark 3"), bty = "n", cex = 0.7)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
}
draw_pca()
save_plot(file.path(cfg$pca, "pc1_pc2.png"), draw_pca, width = 2000)
write.table(plot_data, file.path(cfg$pca, "pca_with_metadata.tsv"), sep = "\t", dec = ".", fileEncoding = "UTF-8", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
```

**Try it yourself — Q5:** describe two features you observe before proposing an
explanation. What additional information would help distinguish population
structure from an array batch effect? Inspect PC2 versus PC3 as well.

## HWE: a diagnostic in controls

Pooled ancestry groups can depart from HWE without a genotyping error. An
association can also generate departures among cases. We therefore first inspect
controls, and discuss population structure before considering exclusions.

```{r pca-hwe-controls}
cohort_fam <- read_fam(cohort)
control_metadata <- join_by_id(cohort_fam[c("FID", "IID")], metadata)
controls <- control_metadata[!is.na(control_metadata$Disease) & control_metadata$Disease == 1, c("FID", "IID")]
if (nrow(controls) < 20) stop("Too few controls for this exercise; review the phenotype coding.")
control_file <- file.path(cfg$pca, "controls.tsv")
write_ids(controls, control_file)
hwe_prefix <- file.path(cfg$pca, "hwe_controls")
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", cohort, "--keep", control_file, "--hardy", "--out", hwe_prefix),
          paste0(hwe_prefix, ".hardy"))
hwe <- read_ws(paste0(hwe_prefix, ".hardy"))
summary(as.numeric(hwe$P))
```

No HWE filter is applied automatically in this walkthrough. Review the controls'
structure and the test counts before choosing a threshold. PCA adjustment in an
association model does not correct a pooled HWE test.

## Build the common analysis sample list

**The question:** can we compare two models without also changing their samples?

```{r pca-covariates}
analysis <- build_covariates(cfg)
table(analysis$Disease)
summary(analysis[c("Age", "SEX", "PC1", "PC2")])
```

**Check your result:** `analysis_samples.tsv` and `covariates.tsv` are saved.
The first file contains FID and IID; the second contains age, sex code and PCs.
Missing values are excluded explicitly, not replaced by zero. Both models in
lesson 3 will use this same complete-case sample set.

**Exit check — Q6:** PCA contains 490 samples, but only 472 have complete age,
sex and phenotype data. How would you make the two association models comparable?
Which file records the decision?

### Going further

- Repeat a control-only HWE diagnostic within a justified study subgroup. To
  filter, create a passing-variant ID list from that diagnostic and apply it to
  the full corresponding case/control cohort. Keep cases in the analysis.
  PLINK 2 does not automatically restrict HWE tests to controls.
- The original course includes a 1000 Genomes exercise. Before merging, confirm
  genome build, variant identity, allele orientation and ambiguous sites. Read
  [reference-panel guidance](../../docs/reference_panel.md). Do not blindly flip all
  mismatching variants or assign ancestry from a two-PC distance rule alone.
- Compare 5 and 10 PCs using a documented sensitivity plan, rather than choosing
  whichever model gives the smallest p-value.
